title: Why is the sum of the cycled numbers divisible by 37?
description: A three digit number is cycled into two more numbers and the three are added. Letters show each digit appears once in every place, so the sum is one hundred eleven times the digit total, and one twenty three checks it.
teaching_notes: One idea: every letter lands once in the hundreds, tens and ones places, so the sum is 111 times the digit total and 111 is 3 times 37. Watch for students who forget that 111 also makes the sum divisible by 3.

video_script.why: The child uses place value with three letters, as in the three digit trick, and sees 111 appear.
video_script.substitution: Write abc, bca and cab by place value, add to get 111a + 111b + 111c, take out 111 = 3 × 37, and check with 123.
video_script.anchor: the three cycled numbers abc, bca and cab written one below the other
video_script.payoff_line: The sum is one hundred eleven times the sum of the digits

final_answer.spoken: one hundred eleven times the sum of the digits

maths_rules: abc = 100a + 10b + c, bca = 100b + 10c + a, cab = 100c + 10a + b
111 = 3 × 37, so the sum is divisible by 37 and by 3
video_script.design: One idea: each letter lands once in each place, so the sum is 111 times the digit total. The three numbers stay on the board and the check is the last step.

narration: <bookmark mark='book'/>This is a question from your book. Take any three digit number with digits eigh, bee and see.
<bookmark mark='cycle'/>Cycle the digits around to make two more numbers, bee see eigh and see eigh bee. Then add all three numbers.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>Why is the sum always divisible by thirty seven? Is it also always divisible by three?

beats.on_screen: the three numbers stay on the board while the child thinks

marks.think: Keeko sits at the corner of the board

beats.on_screen: each letter moves through the hundreds, tens and ones places across the three numbers

marks.plan: arrows show each letter moving through the three places

beats.colours: each letter in its own colour
narration: <bookmark mark='plan'/>We write each number by place value, as in the trick with letters. Each letter will move through the hundreds, tens and ones places.

beats.on_screen: Given: a three digit number abc and its two cycled numbers bca and cab

marks.given: the three numbers are written with letters

narration: <bookmark mark='given'/>Given, a three digit number with digits eigh, bee and see, and its two cycled numbers.

beats.on_screen: To show: the sum is divisible by 37; and to ask whether it is divisible by 3

marks.find: the aim is written on the board

narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to show that thirty seven divides the sum, and then check whether three does too.

beats.on_screen: Step 1: abc = 100a + 10b + c; bca = 100b + 10c + a; cab = 100c + 10a + b
beats.colours: each letter in its own colour
narration: <bookmark mark='first'/>Step one, write the three numbers by place value. The first is one hundred eigh, plus ten bee, plus see.
<bookmark mark='second'/>The second is one hundred bee, plus ten see, plus eigh.
<bookmark mark='third'/>The third is one hundred see, plus ten eigh, plus bee.

marks.group: the a terms, b terms and c terms are grouped

beats.colours: each letter in its own colour
narration: <bookmark mark='group'/>Step two, add the three numbers and group each letter. Eigh appears once as hundreds, once as tens and once as ones.
<bookmark mark='sum'/>That makes one hundred eleven eigh. Bee and see do the same.

marks.common: the common 111 is pulled out in front

beats.colours: the common 111 in the accent colour
narration: <bookmark mark='common'/>Step three, take out one hundred eleven, because all three parts have it.
<bookmark mark='split'/>One hundred eleven is three times thirty seven, so both three and thirty seven divide the sum.
<bookmark mark='add'/>Step four, check with one hundred twenty three. The three numbers add to six hundred sixty six.
<bookmark mark='divide'/>Six hundred sixty six divided by thirty seven is eighteen. Divided by three it is two hundred twenty two.

beats.on_screen: Answer: sum = 111 × (a + b + c), divisible by 37 and by 3

marks.ans: the answer sum = 111 × (a + b + c) is boxed

narration: <bookmark mark='ans'/>The sum is one hundred eleven times the sum of the digits.
<bookmark mark='both'/>Since one hundred eleven is three times thirty seven, thirty seven and three both divide it.
